title: Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press
summary: A plate-loaded shoulder press with independent arms on a slightly forward path.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for front delts (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly front delts total.
Library rating 0.6 for triceps (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly triceps total.
Library rating 0.4 for side delts (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly side delts total.
Library rating 0.3 for traps (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.2 for chest: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly chest total.

setup.text: Set the seat so the handles start at about chin height.
Press up until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower until your hands are at about ear level.

form_cues.cue: Keep the back on the pad
Keep your back on the pad. Don't arch to finish the rep.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back to finish reps.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stable, Linked arm levers, Lower loading potential.
Swap sheet: Less stable, One side at a time, Linked arm levers.
Swap sheet: Less stable, Linked arm levers, More systemic fatigue.
Swap sheet: Linked arm levers, Loads the spine, Heavier loading potential.
